points.t: Pale, pink or fawn macules with **fine bran-like scale** on the upper trunk; noticed after a holiday.
*Malassezia* overgrowth in warm, sweaty, oily skin interferes with melanin.
**Ketoconazole 2% shampoo** as a body wash for 5 days, or an azole cream for small areas.
Not dangerous. Make sure it isn’t **vitiligo** (no scale, chalk-white).

cause.lead: Overgrowth of a yeast everyone carries.
points: Lipophilic *Malassezia* overgrows in sebum-rich skin: chest, back, shoulders, neck.
It **blocks melanin** (pale patches) or inflames mildly (pink-brown patches).
Promoters: heat, humidity, sweat, oily skin, young adulthood; mild immunosuppression.
An overgrowth, **not caught**: not contagious in the usual sense.

features.lead: Colour change with scale you can evoke.
points: Well-demarcated **hypo-, hyper- or pink-fawn** macules merging into patches.
**Fine scale** more obvious when the skin is stretched or scratched (evoked scale).
Upper trunk, shoulders, neck, upper arms.
Usually asymptomatic or mildly itchy; affected skin **doesn’t tan**.

visuals.caption: Typical spread over the upper back and shoulders: small round macules merging into patches, some paler and some pink-brown, with the lower back clear.
visuals.alt: Upper back with pityriasis versicolor patches

items.name: On tanned skin
items.t: Small pale scaly macules; noticed after sun.

points: Scrapings or tape strip: **‘spaghetti and meatballs’** hyphae and spores.

cards.name: Pityriasis alba
cards.clue: Children; ill-defined pale facial patches; atopy.

cards.name: Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation
cards.clue: Previous rash at the same sites; no scale.

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
cards.clue: Greasy scale; scalp, face, central chest.

cards.name: Pityriasis rosea
cards.clue: Herald patch, then ‘Christmas-tree’; settles in 6–8 weeks.

manage.lead: Clear the yeast; colour follows later (CKS).

rx.dose: Once daily; lather, leave 3–5 min, rinse
rx.note: Licensed for this use from age 12.

rx.drug: Azole (clotrimazole, econazole, ketoconazole) or terbinafine cream

points: Oral **itraconazole** or **fluconazole** in adults: check interactions and pregnancy.
Ketoconazole shampoo every 1–4 weeks, or a **3-day course before a sunny holiday**.

limits.t: Colour takes **weeks to months** to return: not treatment failure.
Suggests the infection is still active.

items.t: Diagnostic doubt: especially **no scale** or complete depigmentation (vitiligo).
Very extensive, recurrent or unusual: consider immunosuppression.
Pregnancy or children needing oral therapy: specialist advice.

pearls.t: Warn up front: colour takes **months** to even out.
Not poor hygiene and not usually catching.
Even sun exposure after treatment helps the colour match.
A pre-holiday prophylaxis plan saves repeat visits.

quiz.a: Malassezia, a normal skin yeast, overgrowing.
As a body wash once daily for up to 5 days: lather, leave 3–5 minutes, rinse.

quiz.q: Pale patches but no scale and chalk-white?
Yeast cleared but still pale. Failure?
quiz.a: No: colour takes weeks to months to return.
